subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core expose cross-gateway session control through `gateway.peers` and model-facing session tool parameters, or should this wait for a narrower peer/federation contract?
rationale: The code choice changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, transcript visibility, and whether agents can direct authenticated Gateway traffic to non-local endpoints.

options.title: Define the core peer contract first
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and visibility contract before accepting core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Narrow this PR to configured peers only
options.body: Remove raw `gatewayUrl` from model-facing session tools and allow only configured peers after fixing protocol and validation bugs.

options.title: Defer to the federation FRD
options.body: Keep this PR paused or closed until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 settles the bridge protocol and operator-scope model.

recommendation.title: Define the core peer contract first
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-approved identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and visibility contract before accepting core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for session tools and gatewayUrl security routes this decision to steipete.
